info.desc: To Pimp a Butterfly is the third studio album by American hip-hop artist, Kendrick Lamar. The album was released on March 16, 2015, by Top Dawg Entertainment, Aftermath Entertainment, and distributed by Interscope Records. Upon its release, "To Pimp a Butterfly" received rave reviews from music critics. Lamar has described the album, which incorporates elements of funk, spoken word poetry and jazz, as "honest, fearful and unapologetic." In an interview with Rolling Stone magazine, Kendrick indicated that the title was a play on Harper Lee's novel "To Kill a Mockingbird". He was quoted as saying, "Just putting the word 'pimp' .

podcast.body: David Bowie regarded this album as an "authentic masterpiece" and listened to it continuously, highlighting its crucial influence on the sound and direction of his final album, Black Star. It is considered essential listening to understand Black Star. "para el la grandísima obra, que consideraba posiblemente no de los mejores discos de los últimos años era Tu Pimp a Butterfly de Kendrick Lamar, este álbum para él era una auténtica obra maestra y lo escuchaba de manera continuada."

This LP was defeated by repeat winner Taylor Swift's "1989" at the 2016 Grammys. It was argued that not giving the prize to a repeat winner "might have gotten Kendrick Lamar a Grammy" in this instance. "Kendrick Lamar a Grammy in 2016 for his to pimp a butterfly LP, which was defeated by repeat winner Taylor Swift."

podcast.body: This acclaimed 2015 album was among Kendrick Lamar's "Grammy-winning chart-topping albums." It notably produced his "Black Lives Matter anthem 'Alright'," showcasing his evolving artistic and social commentary. "2015's To Pimp A Butterfly, which produced his Black Lives Matter anthem All Right."

podcast.body: This album is widely considered by critics to be the most important album of the 21st century. Its gestation began in 2013 during Kenny West's famous Jesus tour, which Kendrick Lamar participated in. The creation of the album involved a complex idea from Kendrick Lamar, who dedicated two years to traveling the world to find the right collaborators. He acted as a "master of ceremonies," bringing together over 100 artists, with 65 officially credited, to contribute to his clear vision for the album. The album transcends traditional rap, incorporating Jazz, Funk, deep Soul, Avant-Garde, and Reggae, synthesizing 50 years of musical genius into just over an hour of music. "considerado por gran parte de la crítica en el álbum más importante del siglo XXI."
